summary: The Wildlife Crossings Program Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes and updates the existing wildlife crossings program. It authorizes $100,000,000 per year from the Highway Trust Fund for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, adjusts cost-share requirements for certain communities, provides tribal technical assistance, and allows for grant administration funding.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for a 90 percent Federal share for project costs, which may be increased up to 100 percent by the Secretary in cases of financial hardship.
Eligible for technical and application assistance funded by up to 0.5 percent of program funds to improve funding access.

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations of $100,000,000 annually from the Highway Trust Fund for the wildlife crossings program for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
Makes appropriated funds available until expended.
Removes the word 'pilot' from the program title and references in title 23, United States Code.
Establishes a 90 percent Federal cost share for grants benefiting small, rural, and disadvantaged communities, which the Secretary may raise to 100 percent in cases of financial hardship.
Allows the Secretary to use up to 0.5 percent of program funds for tribal technical assistance and application support.
Allows the Secretary to retain up to 0.5 percent of program funds for grant administration and application review.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Wildlife Crossings Program Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes and updates the existing wildlife crossings program. It authorizes $100,000,000 per year from the Highway Trust Fund for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, adjusts cost-share requirements for certain communities, provides tribal technical assistance, and allows for grant administration funding.
summary_detail.significance: The bill continues and updates funding for wildlife crossing projects by authorizing $100 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, while adjusting cost-sharing rules to assist small, rural, and disadvantaged communities and providing technical assistance for tribal entities.
